questions.question_text:
An account begins with $\$8000$ and receives regular deposits of $\$500$ at the end of each year for $6\text{ years}$ at $5\%$ p.a. compounded annually.
Find the future value of the account.

options.why: Calculated compound interest on the lump sum alone without adding the annuity series.
Added principal contributions ($8000 + 3000$) without calculating compound interest.
Subtracted the annuity series from the lump sum instead of adding it.

questions.question_text:
A retirement account starts with $\$80\,000$ earning $6\%$ p.a. compounded monthly.
At the end of each month, $\$900$ is withdrawn.
Calculate the balance remaining in the account after $5\text{ years}$.

options.why: Added the annuity series to the compounded principal instead of subtracting withdrawals.
Subtracted simple total withdrawals ($80000 - 54000$) without compound interest.
Calculated withdrawals using annual periods instead of monthly compounding.

questions.question_text:
An investor deposits $\$15\,000$ initially and adds $\$300$ at the end of each month for $3\text{ years}$ into an account earning $7.2\%$ p.a. compounded monthly.
Find the final balance.

options.why: Compounded the initial $\$15\,000$ but omitted the monthly annuity contributions.
Summed the uncompounded cash deposits ($15000 + 36 \times 300$).
Subtracted the annuity contributions from the compounded lump sum.

questions.question_text:
A person wants to invest a single lump sum $PV$ into an account earning $4.8\%$ p.a. compounded monthly in order to withdraw $\$1500$ at the end of each month for $8\text{ years}$ ($n=96$), leaving a balance of $\$0$.
Find the required lump sum $PV$.

options.why: Multiplied $\$1500$ by 96 months without accounting for interest earned during drawdown.
Calculated the future value of payments instead of discounting back to present value.
Discounted the simple sum of withdrawals ($\$144\,000$) instead of the compound annuity series.

questions.question_text:
A fund begins with $\$40\,000$ and earns $6\%$ p.a. compounded monthly.
If $\$1000$ is withdrawn at the end of each month, how many complete withdrawals of $\$1000$ can be made in full?

options.why: Rounded up to 45, but the 45th withdrawal cannot be made in full because the remaining balance is only about $\$737$.
Divided $\$40\,000$ by $\$1000$ without accounting for interest earned during the drawdown period.
Subtracted $1$ on the wrong side when rearranging the logarithmic equation.

questions.question_text:
A company sets up an equipment maintenance fund with an initial $\$60\,000$ earning $5.4\%$ p.a. compounded monthly.
At the end of each month, $\$1200$ is withdrawn for servicing.
Calculate the balance of the fund after $4\text{ years}$.

options.why: Added the withdrawal series to the compounded principal instead of subtracting it.
Subtracted uncompounded withdrawals ($60000 - 48 \times 1200$) without interest.
Compounded the initial deposit but omitted the monthly withdrawals.

questions.question_text:
A retiree has $\$250\,000$ in a fund earning $6\%$ p.a. compounded monthly.
What is the maximum monthly withdrawal $M$ she can make at the end of each month so that the fund lasts exactly $15\text{ years}$ ($n=180$)?

options.why: Divided $\$250\,000$ by 180 months without accounting for compound interest earned.
Calculated simple interest plus principal divided by the number of periods.
Treated withdrawals as start-of-month payments rather than end-of-month payments.

questions.question_text:
A scholarship fund starts with $\$120\,000$ earning $4.8\%$ p.a. compounded monthly.
If $\$1400$ is withdrawn at the end of each month, which equation correctly models the number of months $n$ until the fund is exhausted?

options.why: Inverted the fraction when rearranging the drawdown equation.
Divided monthly withdrawal directly by the initial balance without compounding.
Used the annual interest rate of $4.8\%$ instead of the monthly rate of $0.4\%$.
